description: Protocol v1 section 23. Which vector files a mobile SDK (the native iOS and Android SDKs, and so the Flutter and React Native wrappers over them) must pass. Every file in this directory appears once. `required` files are run by each native SDK's tests; `n/a` files cover server-side or web-only behaviour a mobile SDK does not implement. Hand-maintained: the protocol tests fail when a vector file is missing from it or listed twice.

suites.why: server-side account hashing; an SDK never hashes account ids
assessment ids are sealed and read by the server only
the binding bytes B, request hash and client data hash are built natively on both platforms
the action and cdata charsets, which an SDK validates before sending
web hostname binding; an app challenge carries an app id, not a hostname
site-key format only (the `siteKey` cases); secret and management keys never reach an app

both directions of the bridge: parseCases for the page-to-native message validator, nativeCases for the messages an SDK sends to the page (each outgoing message must parse), and urlCases for the hosted page URL
Play Integrity and App Attest error mapping, and the reading of API responses
sha256-v1 proof of work is solved natively on both platforms
puzzle schemas; the native sheet sends the puzzle fields the page reads (mobile-bridge nativeCases), and mobile-client covers the solve response
reason codes are read by relying parties, not by an SDK
the server SDK conformance manifest; a mobile SDK is not a server SDK
server SDK HTTP behaviour (siteverify calls and retries); a mobile SDK calls the app endpoints instead
server SDK response schemas for siteverify; a mobile SDK never calls siteverify
